axis_set: A. Purpose of education (two historical tracks)
definition: Education viewed through an economic lens: human capital theory, education for the economy; GDP growth as main policy objective
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Does our curriculum frame AI literacy mainly as workforce/economic preparation?

axis_set: A. Purpose of education (two historical tracks)
definition: Education for human development: meeting basic human needs, enlarging individual/social/political freedoms; capability approach
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Does our curriculum also serve non-instrumental aims (flourishing, freedom, citizenship)?

axis_set: B. Three categories of what constitutes 'good'
definition: Relationships with family members, friends, community members, citizens, animals and the environment
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), p.105
original_source: WG1-ch2 explication of 'good for all human beings'
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Which relationships does the curriculum cultivate (peers, teachers, AI agents, nature)? Does it treat AI chatbots as relationship partners and problematize that?

axis_set: B. Three categories of what constitutes 'good'
definition: Meaningful engagement in activities such as play, work, learning, caring
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), p.105
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Are students genuinely engaged in worthwhile activities (not just busy)? Which activities do learning points create?

axis_set: B. Three categories of what constitutes 'good'
definition: Capacity to act, choose and control who one aspires to be; not totally predetermined by external conditions
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), p.105
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do students gain agency over AI (choose when/how to use it, resist manipulation) or only knowledge about it?

definition: Optimal continuing development of human potential and living well: engagement in relationships and activities that are meaningful (aligned with own values and humanistic values) and satisfying; encompasses uniqueness, dignity, diversity, freedom, happiness, holistic well-being within community
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022); Synopsis Duraiappah & van Atteveldt (2022)
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Is flourishing an explicit aim of the curriculum, or only competence/safety?

definition: Possibility: if conditions are right, the person could do/become x; only denies that they cannot
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), pp.99-101
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Does the curriculum assume all students can learn AI concepts given conditions (vs tracking by presumed ability)?

definition: Conditionally predictable endpoint/disposition: will reach x if conditions present; trait-like (cf. character strengths)
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), pp.99-101
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do we build dispositions (e.g. habit of verifying AI outputs) or only one-off performances?

definition: Effectiveness in promoting a designated outcome; what is within a person's power to do and what they are free to do; predicted to become x if they make the effort
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), pp.99-101
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Can students actually do the thing (catch a hallucination, verify a claim) when they choose to?

definition: What people actually do or have; realized achievements
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: What do our MC items measure: realized functioning under test conditions only?

definition: The range of possibilities from which people can choose their functionings; substantive freedoms/opportunities
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do we measure the opportunities/freedoms students gain (what they could do), not only what they did on the test?

definition: Self-directedness congruent with personal values and sense of self
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do students make self-endorsed choices about AI use, or only follow rules?

definition: Sense of mastery: experiencing oneself as capable over activities one considers important
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do lessons give experiences of mastery (IMI perceived competence shows partial signal)?

definition: Being positively related to others; supportive social climate and relationships
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Does the curriculum support peer/teacher relatedness (grouping, collaboration) or isolate?

definition: Extension of autonomy: engaging in activities that take one beyond self - prosocial behaviour, arts, nature, contemplative practice
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Does AI literacy connect to beyond-self concerns (society, others affected by AI) or stay self-focused?

definition: Extension of competence: need for wisdom about how to live a good life and be fully human; reflective exploration of big questions of life and death
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do lessons touch big questions (what AI means for a good life) or only technical know-how?

definition: Extension of relatedness: contributing significantly to one's ingroups, strangers and society at large; feeling that what one does matters
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do students' AI projects matter to someone (real audience, contribution) or are they throwaway exercises?

definition: Attention control, emotion regulation, goal focus; underlies learning to know/think, do/evaluate, learn
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do lessons train or overload self-regulation (cognitive load, distraction by tools)?

definition: Overarching state/trait integrating 5 dimensions: self-other-world focus; connection vs disconnect; solidity vs flexibility of self (decentering); agency; sense-of-purpose locus (self vs self-transcending)
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Does AI use expand self-world (connection, flexible self, purpose beyond self) or narrow it (sycophancy, self-focus)?

definition: Relationship with nature and the more-than-human world; capacities to conserve the environment
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Is AI's environmental cost / sustainability addressed?

definition: Engagement with past and present human achievements (humanities, arts, sciences); capabilities to benefit from and contribute to culture (critical thinking, cultural literacy)
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Is AI content linked to cultural knowledge and critical thinking, or taught as isolated tech skill?

definition: Society, norms, job market; citizenship; social inclusion
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Are societal impacts of AI (bias, labour, democracy) covered?

definition: Internet, social networks, AI, etc.; relationship with technology
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Core home domain of our curriculum - is it balanced against the other five?

definition: Relationships with others; education as relationship
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do lessons address how AI mediates/changes interpersonal relationships (chatbots as companions)?

definition: Oneself (body, mind); inner life, self-knowledge
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do students reflect on their own AI use, emotions, vulnerabilities (socio-affective pull)?

definition: Knowledge acquisition plus higher-order thinking ('to think' added post-Delors)
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our battery's strength - but Bloom bottom-heavy (1 Evaluate item)

definition: Practical skills plus evaluation judgement ('evaluate' added post-Delors)
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do students practise doing (build, prompt, verify) and evaluating outputs?

definition: Metacognition, self-regulated learning; own trajectory due to internet autodidactic learning
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do students learn how to keep learning about AI after the unit ends (moving target)?

definition: Citizenship, living with others; manifestation of mattering and wisdom needs
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: MAIL 'Participate & Collaborate' = 0 in our curriculum - known gap

definition: New pillar: harmonious relationship with environment
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Absent from our curriculum (AI & environment not taught)

definition: Identity exploration and expansion beyond self-focus; linked to self-transcendence
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Does the curriculum touch identity (who am I with/as AI user)?

definition: Autonomy, mastery, relatedness map onto self-regulatory capacity and onto learning to know/think, do/evaluate, learn
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Cross-check: do our knowledge-focused weeks also serve autonomy/mastery/relatedness?

definition: Self-transcendence, wisdom, mattering map onto self-world capacity and onto learning to live together, live with nature, be and become
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Cross-check: the self-world cluster is exactly where our curriculum is thinnest

definition: Relationships/activities must be a source of significance - the feeling that what one does matters
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), pp.105-107
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Are learning points significant to students' lives now (they already use chatbots)?

definition: Stable intention to accomplish something meaningful to the self and consequential for the world beyond the self
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), pp.105-107
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do activities connect to purpose beyond the classroom?

definition: Activity must align with the person's deepest values AND humanistic values; meaning arises when subjective attraction meets objective attractiveness
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), pp.105-107
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Is AI use framed by values (honesty, fairness, wellbeing) not only rules?

definition: Being free from inappropriate interference from others
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), p.107
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do students learn freedom-from AI harms (manipulation, surveillance, sycophancy)?

definition: Being free to engage in activities and relationships
source_chapter: WG1-ch2 De Ruyter et al. (2022), p.107
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do students learn freedom-to use AI for their own flourishing (creation, learning)?

definition: The intended, policy-level curriculum
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our Sense-A coding of the designed curriculum (slide decks, plans)

definition: The curriculum as actually enacted by teachers
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our enactment data (pacing overruns, W7 asymmetry Build vs Control)

definition: What is actually tested
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our coverage check: 17/51 learning points assessed (33%)

definition: Unintended messages transmitted by structure/practice
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: What do our lessons implicitly teach (e.g. AI as authority if outputs never questioned)?

definition: Students' inner experience during learning
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Partially captured by weekly IMI (enjoyment, pressure)

definition: What is omitted from the curriculum
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our reverse-coverage analysis (sycophancy never taught; MAIL Participate & Collaborate = 0)

definition: Active meaning-making situated in context
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do we analyse the learning process or only outcomes?

definition: First-person and collective experience shaped by spaces and relationships
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: IMI weekly + teacher pulse capture experience; analysed as own outcome

definition: Relatively permanent changes in: dispositions, capabilities, knowledge, behaviours, values, attitudes, preferences
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our battery measures knowledge only; dispositions/behaviours/values unmeasured

definition: Expected end result: development of capacities, propensities and capabilities contributing to flourishing of self and others
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Are our learning points linked to stated capability aims?

definition: Potential must be translated into action; contributing to flourishing of broader interpersonal circles and conditions that facilitate flourishing
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do we observe enactment (students actually verifying, protecting themselves) or only potential?

definition: Assessment as constant part of curriculum/teaching and of life (feedback on progression), not an external supervisor of education
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our formative_check coding + Sense-B audit align; is assessment used for learning or only for research?

dimension: Measure positive skills, not absence of ill-health
definition: Flourishing assessment should assess positive skills and qualities, not merely absence of mental ill-health
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our affect battery measures positive states (interest/enjoyment) - aligned

definition: Assessing underlying capacities as concise predictors of a range of flourishing skills and qualities
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Could a small set of capacity measures (e.g. calibration/IDK propensity) predict many learning outcomes?

definition: Repeated assessments of the same participants to infer developmental change; RCT gold standard but naturalistic implementation studies increasingly valued
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our T1/T4/T7 repeated design aligns; T8 delayed wave still pending

definition: Informed consent from parents, assent from adolescents, data handling, who accesses individual flourishing data
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Covered by ETH Zurich approval 25 ETHICS-247; teacher access to individual data unresolved

definition: Volatility, uncertainty, complexity and ambiguity as central characteristics of the world education must address
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our 'moving target' argument (prompt engineering 2025 to context engineering 2026) is exactly VUCA

definition: Teacher-student and peer relationships as foundation of flourishing schools
source_chapter: WG1-ch5 Flook, O'Toole, Ritter & Schonert-Reichl (2022), p.251
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Do lessons build peer/teacher relationships (grouping coded in Pedagogy)?

definition: Self-knowledge, self-compassion, inner life
analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Any self-reflection on own AI use built in?

definition: Forming a healthy lifelong relationship with knowledge (not boredom/antagonism)
source_chapter: WG1-ch5 Flook et al. (2022), p.251; WG1-ch4

analysis_question_for_our_curriculum: Our five dimensions (Context, Content, Pedagogy, Didactics, Assessment) can be cross-walked to WG1-WG4
